template.name: Mindray AniFM I1 Infusion Pump
template.desc: Mindray AniFM I1 veterinary infusion pump (Class I, internal battery). From the CHS Ansur template “0000 -AniFM I1 0000000000 EST+PVT AS-NZS 3551 DD.MM.YYYY.mtt” (file name), checked against the I1 Service Manual H-046-00589A-00 (ch. 3.3 and 4) and the I1 Operator’s Manual H-046-00375A-00 (App. A). Electrical safety to AS/NZS 3551:2012+A2. Changed from Ansur: earth leakage NC 5000, ON 10000 µA (B11.6; Ansur 500 / 1000 µA). Changed from Ansur: accuracy readings are the delivered volume in mL (19–21 and 57–63 mL, the manual’s ±5 %; Ansur gave % with 95–105). Changed from Ansur: occlusion pressure is in mmHg, 400–650 (Ansur kPa 53–87 is the same range: 400–650 mmHg is 53.3–86.7 kPa). Changed from Ansur: the push-pull box item removed (syringe pump wording, the I1 has none); beep wording corrected (speaker two, buzzer three); door, pressure block, anti-free-flow, bubble, drop sensor and label checks added from the manual; ESA612 tests moved after the power-on test; service passwords left out of the text (they are in the service manual). Kept as in Ansur, differs from the manual (for Jonathan to confirm): no patient leakage or mains-on-applied-part test and no applied part group, because the service manual says the applied part (syringe or infusion set) is non-metallic with no electrical connection, although the operator’s manual and data sheet class the pump as Type CF. Kept as in Ansur, differs from the manual (for Jonathan to confirm): earth leakage keeps the AS/NZS 3551 limits; the service manual (electrical safety test and test report form) gives a much tighter manufacturer limit of not more than 347 µA in normal condition and 694 µA in single fault (zero line open), measured with an AC+DC leakage test to IEC 60601-1. Kept as in Ansur, differs from the manual (for Jonathan to confirm): the occlusion pressure limit is 400–650 mmHg as in the procedure (Table 3-2); the manual’s test report form says 425–725 mmHg. Unverified: whether the I1 can be set to exactly 525 mmHg (its operator’s manual lists occlusion levels, default P3 = 600 mmHg).

items: The parts of the pump are complete, without physical damage (enclosure, LCD, buttons), and nothing rattles when the pump is shaken
Power interface: no rust, foreign matter or trace of burning
The power cord is not damaged and plugs in tightly
Drop sensor (if fitted): complete without cracks, springs back when pressed, cable undamaged and plugged in tightly
The fastening clamp is complete, without cracks, and holds the pump firmly on the infusion stand
Data interfaces (multifunction connector, USB-C): undamaged, no drug residue, and the USB-C protection cap is present
The safety label and nameplate are clear and undamaged
Connected to AC power, the AC power indicator and the battery indicator light up
At power-on the speaker gives two beeps (Di-Di) and the buzzer, if fitted, gives three beeps (Di-Di-Di)
During power-on the red and yellow alarm indicators flash in sequence
The Guide to Load the Infusion Set screen is displayed
Press the Open button: the door opens automatically; when closed it locks automatically
There is no alarm during the power-on operation
On AC power (with the battery fitted) the pump works normally
With the AC cord removed the pump keeps working and shows Battery in Use; then reconnect the cord

steps.title: Mains voltage
steps.instructions: Plug the ESA612 into the mains supply you are testing from.

steps.title: Protective earth resistance
steps.instructions: Connect the pump’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to the equipotential terminal or an exposed earthed metal part of the pump. Limit 0.2 Ω (AS/NZS 3551 B8.6; the service manual also says less than 0.2 Ω).

steps.title: Insulation: mains to non-earth accessible conductive part
steps.instructions: Connect the pump’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet and switch the pump on. Don’t touch the pump during the test.

steps.title: Enclosure leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the pump’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to metal foil wrapped around the (plastic) enclosure, or to an exposed unearthed metal part. Limits 100 / 500 / 500 µA (AS/NZS 3551 B10.5).

steps.title: Earth leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the pump’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. The pump will be switched on and off between conditions. Limits 5000 µA normal, 10000 µA neutral open (AS/NZS 3551 B11.6).

steps.title: Functionality test
steps.instructions: Service Manual 3.3.5.1 (p.17–19) and 4.4 (p.33–34). Use an infusion set, tertiary test water or saline.

items: System date and time agree with the local time
Each button rebounds normally and the pump responds
Door pressure blocks (2 for ultrasonic, 2 for pressure): each spring returns to position when pressed
After an infusion set is loaded, its brand appears in the list of brands
Anti-free-flow: load a water-filled set but do not start: no fluid comes out of the end of the set

Normal infusion: load the set, set the parameters and press Start: the pump runs without obvious jitter or abnormal noise, and the running icon, rate, volume and pressure values are displayed correctly
Audible and visual alarms at all levels work; the volume control and the alarm mute work
Occlusion alarm: run at 100 mL/h and block the lower end of the set by hand: a downstream occlusion alarm sounds within 5 minutes
Bubble alarm: run at 100 mL/h and turn the drip chamber to make a bubble of about 1–2 cm: a high-priority bubble alarm sounds and the pump stops

Drop sensor (if fitted): start an infusion with the sensor on the drip chamber, then remove it: the pump stops within 2 minutes, the alarm sounds, the indicator flashes red and Empty is shown on the LCD
The LCD is not blurred or garbled and the touchscreen responds normally

steps.title: Calibration to the customer’s infusion set (only if needed)
steps.instructions:
Needed when the pump is first used, with a new brand of infusion set, after repair, or when the accuracy or occlusion pressure test fails (Service Manual 3.3.1–3.3.2, p.12–14; 4.3, p.29). Otherwise mark both items N/A.
Accuracy calibration: needs a 500 g electronic balance, a 100 mL beaker and the infusion set; use saline, glucose solution or grade III water; remove the needle and keep the end of the set below the liquid level in the beaker. Menu > Manufacturer Maint. > (service password, see the service manual) > Accuracy Calibration > Start Calibration, select the brand. Hold Bolus to purge into the beaker. Press Start/Stop for the automatic run, weigh the liquid and enter it as Volume 1, press OK, run again and enter Volume 2, press OK.
Pressure calibration: Menu > Manufacturer Maint. > (service password) > Pressure Calibration, select the brand, connect the set to an approved pressure gauge. Press Start/Stop; at 150 mmHg press Start/Stop again to collect, then enter the stable gauge value. Repeat at 500 mmHg until Calib done is shown. This screen has no occlusion alarm: never infuse an animal from it.

items: Accuracy calibration to the customer’s infusion set done (N/A if not needed)
Pressure calibration to the customer’s infusion set done (N/A if not needed)

steps.title: Performance test
steps.instructions:
Service Manual 3.3.3 (p.14–16) and 4.4 (p.34).
Accuracy test: use the same platform as the accuracy calibration, open the door and use a different section of the tube. Weigh the empty beaker, put the end of the set against the wall of the beaker, set the rate and VTBI, and start the timer as the infusion starts. When it finishes, check the timed duration equals the time the pump calculated, release any drop on the needle into the beaker, weigh and enter the water delivered (1 g of water = 1 mL). Acceptance is ±5 %.
Occlusion pressure test: connect the set to a pressure gauge in peak mode (or an infusion analyser) at the same height as the pump and purge by gravity. Set the occlusion pressure to 525 mmHg (Table 3-2; the I1 operator’s manual lists occlusion levels rather than mmHg values, default P3 = 600 mmHg, so if 525 mmHg cannot be set, note the level used), run at 100 mL/h unblocked, then close the three-way tap (or trigger the analyser). When the occlusion alarm sounds, enter the peak pressure. If a reading is out, repeat the calibration.

readings.label: Accuracy: 200 mL/h, VTBI 20 mL, 6 min: delivered volume 19–21 mL (±5 %)
Accuracy: 1200 mL/h, VTBI 60 mL, 3 min: delivered volume 57–63 mL (±5 %)
Occlusion pressure: 100 mL/h, set 525 mmHg: peak pressure at the alarm 400–650 mmHg
